answer: One applicant takes a numbered quill at a scriptorium, pays 90 dollars, and posts 150 tokens for 120 days. A scribe cuts the nib to a unique pattern. Each morning the applicant writes one dated line in iron-gall ink in a bound ledger, then presses a rye kernel into the wax anchor seal. A warden checks the handwriting twice, and a forged line forfeits the deposit and bars the applicant 180 days. Forging 10,000 identities freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. A copied page stands out like a forged signature in a parish register, and the scribe strikes the name from the roll.
